Facts: The mother and daughter of the deceased sought declaration that a transfer of bare ownership with reserved usufruct concealed a donation infringing their reserved shares, requesting restitution or monetary reinstatement; the defendant objected that the action for reduction was inadmissible for lack of acceptance with benefit of inventory.

Legal framework
Articles 476, 484–493 and 564 ICC on tacit acceptance, acceptance with benefit of inventory and conditions for the action for reduction; Articles 553–556 ICC on reduction of donations; consolidated Supreme Court case law on totally pretermitted heirs and simulation actions ancillary to reduction.

Interpretative issue
Whether the plaintiffs qualified as totally pretermitted heirs exempt from acceptance with benefit of inventory, and whether acts concerning inherited movable property constituted tacit acceptance barring the reduction action.

Principle applied
Acceptance with benefit of inventory is a condition of admissibility for the action for reduction when it is brought against non-heirs, including where simulation is alleged solely to support reduction. The exemption applies only to totally pretermitted heirs who are materially unable to perform acts of acceptance. Acts implying control and disposition of inherited assets—such as registration and transfer of a registered movable property—constitute tacit acceptance of the inheritance under Article 476 ICC. Once tacit acceptance has occurred, the heir cannot validly bring a reduction action without prior acceptance with benefit of inventory, rendering the claim inadmissible.
